findings.body: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` is raised before pagination, turning a previously working audit-log listing into an unhandled 500 error.
findings.failure_mode: Unhandled exception during request handling (HTTP 500) for token-authenticated or membership-less contexts.
findings.impact: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access'` is raised before pagination, turning a previously working audit-log listing into an unhandled 500 error.
findings.root_cause: New permission expression dereferences `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member`, which is declared as `RpcOrganizationMember | None`, without a None check.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the member access, e.g. `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or bool(organization_context.member and organization_context.member.has_global_access)`, and only evaluate it inside the `use_optimized` branch.
findings.title: Unguarded `organization_context.member` dereference can raise AttributeError
findings.trigger: Any GET to the audit-log endpoint where `request.user.is_superuser` is falsy and `organization_context.member` is None (e.g. org auth token / integration token auth, or a user context without an active membership row). The expression is evaluated unconditionally on every request, not only when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 71 verbatim shows `organization_context.member.has_global_access` without a None check. RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is declared as `RpcOrganizationMember | None` (model.py:346). When member is None (token auth, no membership), AttributeError is raised unconditionally before pagination.

raw_findings.body: Invalid cursors no longer surface as errors for forward paging (the first page is silently returned, and the derived next/prev cursors are computed from a different offset than requested), while prev cursors still fail with Django's negative-indexing ValueError — two different behaviors for the same invalid input.
raw_findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
raw_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent handling of invalid cursor input: silent wrong-page results in one path, unhandled exception in the other.
raw_findings.impact: Invalid cursors no longer surface as errors for forward paging (the first page is silently returned, and the derived next/prev cursors are computed from a different offset than requested), while prev cursors still fail with Django's negative-indexing ValueError — two different behaviors for the same invalid input.
raw_findings.root_cause: Partial offset normalization was added on one branch of a conditional expression while the prev-cursor path and the downstream `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check keep using the raw offset.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle negative offsets uniformly: validate once at the top of `get_result` and raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")` (as `OffsetPaginator` does) instead of clamping only the non-prev branch.
raw_findings.title: Silent clamping of negative offsets contradicts the added comment and is inconsistent for prev cursors
raw_findings.trigger: A client supplies a cursor with a negative offset to any `BasePaginator` subclass (e.g. `DateTimePaginator`). Forward cursors are now silently rewritten to offset 0, while prev cursors (`is_prev=True`) still pass the negative offset into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two comment lines, or replace them with an explicit validation such as rejecting `offset < 0` if negative offsets are truly unsupported.

raw_findings.body: The configured `self.max_segment_spans` is now never read anywhere (the Python-side enforcement was deleted), so the option silently has no effect and the effective cap is always 1000, off by one from the previous default of 1001.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Configuration is silently ignored; operators cannot tune the segment span cap.
raw_findings.impact: The configured `self.max_segment_spans` is now never read anywhere (the Python-side enforcement was deleted), so the option silently has no effect and the effective cap is always 1000, off by one from the previous default of 1001.
raw_findings.root_cause: Enforcement moved from Python to Lua without threading the existing configuration value through, leaving a magic constant and an orphaned setting.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the limit into the script as an ARGV (e.g. `local max_spans = tonumber(ARGV[5])`) from `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans`, or remove the now-unused `max_segment_spans` constructor parameter.
raw_findings.title: Segment span cap hardcoded to 1000 in Lua, making `max_segment_spans` dead configuration
raw_findings.trigger: Constructing `SpansBuffer(max_segment_spans=N)` with any N other than the hardcoded 1000 (the default is 1001) and ingesting a segment with more than 1000 spans.

raw_findings.body: Span data is dropped with no `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` counter and no log line, so oversized-segment truncation becomes invisible in monitoring and dashboards/alerts built on that metric go permanently to zero.
raw_findings.evidence:

                    logger.error("Skipping too large segment, span count %s", len(payloads[key]))
raw_findings.impact: Span data is dropped with no `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` counter and no log line, so oversized-segment truncation becomes invisible in monitoring and dashboards/alerts built on that metric go permanently to zero.
raw_findings.root_cause: The Python-side span-count enforcement, together with its metric and log, was removed while the replacement eviction in Lua added no observability.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return the number of evicted members from the Lua script (zpopmin's reply length) and emit a metric such as `spans.buffer.process_spans.spans_evicted` in `process_spans`, or keep an equivalent counter on the flush path.
raw_findings.title: Span eviction no longer emits a metric or log when spans are dropped
raw_findings.trigger: A trace whose segment accumulates more than 1000 spans; the new `zpopmin` in add-buffer.lua discards the excess spans during insert.

raw_findings.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so the duplicated member's score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values (roughly 2x epoch seconds). That member is then treated as the newest span and is never evicted by `zpopmin`, while genuinely newer spans get evicted instead.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Incorrect eviction ordering and corrupted score values for duplicated span payloads.
raw_findings.impact: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so the duplicated member's score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values (roughly 2x epoch seconds). That member is then treated as the newest span and is never evicted by `zpopmin`, while genuinely newer spans get evicted instead.
raw_findings.root_cause: Migration from SUNIONSTORE to ZUNIONSTORE relied on the default SUM aggregation, which is meaningless for timestamp scores.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Specify the aggregation explicitly: `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key, "AGGREGATE", "MAX")` (same for the parent_key union).
raw_findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation corrupts span timestamp scores for duplicate payloads
raw_findings.trigger: The same span payload is present in both `set_key` and `span_key` (or `parent_key`) — e.g. a duplicated/retried span that was buffered under two ids before the redirect merge.

raw_findings.body: Segment trees deeper than 1000 stop being joined correctly, producing split/duplicated segments; the change is unrelated to the eviction feature and the comment documenting this exact limitation was removed, so the tradeoff is no longer discoverable.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent behavioral regression for deep segment trees with no documentation of the new limit.
raw_findings.impact: Segment trees deeper than 1000 stop being joined correctly, producing split/duplicated segments; the change is unrelated to the eviction feature and the comment documenting this exact limitation was removed, so the tradeoff is no longer discoverable.
raw_findings.root_cause: Loop upper bound lowered by an order of magnitude alongside deletion of the comment that documented the consequence.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 10000 bound (and its explanatory comment) or, if the reduction is intentional, keep an equivalent comment documenting that redirect chains deeper than 1000 may not be joined and justify the change in the PR.
raw_findings.title: Redirect-chain loop bound silently reduced from 10000 to 1000 and its caveat comment deleted
raw_findings.trigger: Ingesting a trace whose redirect chain (segment tree depth) exceeds 1000 hops, which previously still resolved because the loop allowed up to 10000 iterations.

raw_findings.body: Regressions in the eviction logic (wrong count argument, evicting the root span, off-by-one at the boundary) ship undetected.

raw_findings.root_cause: New eviction behavior added in Lua without an accompanying integration test at the SpansBuffer level.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a buffer test that inserts >1000 spans with increasing `end_timestamp_precise` into one segment and asserts that `flush_segments` returns exactly 1000 spans and that the lowest-timestamp spans were dropped.
raw_findings.title: No test covers the new >1000-span eviction path
raw_findings.trigger: Running the updated test suite: `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` only exercises segments of a handful of spans, and the previous Python-side span-count limit had no test either (`max_segment_spans` has no matches under `tests/sentry`), so the new eviction branch is never executed.

finding.body: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so the duplicated member's score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values (roughly 2x epoch seconds). That member is then treated as the newest span and is never evicted by `zpopmin`, while genuinely newer spans get evicted instead.
finding.failure_mode: Incorrect eviction ordering and corrupted score values for duplicated span payloads.
finding.impact: ZUNIONSTORE defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so the duplicated member's score becomes the sum of two `end_timestamp_precise` values (roughly 2x epoch seconds). That member is then treated as the newest span and is never evicted by `zpopmin`, while genuinely newer spans get evicted instead.
finding.root_cause: Migration from SUNIONSTORE to ZUNIONSTORE relied on the default SUM aggregation, which is meaningless for timestamp scores.
finding.suggested_fix: Specify the aggregation explicitly: `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key, "AGGREGATE", "MAX")` (same for the parent_key union).
finding.title: ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregation corrupts span timestamp scores for duplicate payloads
finding.trigger: The same span payload is present in both `set_key` and `span_key` (or `parent_key`) — e.g. a duplicated/retried span that was buffered under two ids before the redirect merge.
finding.verifier_reason: Lines 47 and 53 show `zunionstore` without AGGREGATE argument. Redis ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM. If same member exists in both sets, scores (timestamps) are summed, corrupting the eviction ordering based on end_timestamp_precise.

rejected_findings.reason: 0.800 is below 0.920: Lines 47 and 53 show `zunionstore` without AGGREGATE argument. Redis ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM. If same member exists in both sets, scores (timestamps) are summed, corrupting the eviction ordering based on end_timestamp_precise.

validated_findings.body: Invalid cursors no longer surface as errors for forward paging (the first page is silently returned, and the derived next/prev cursors are computed from a different offset than requested), while prev cursors still fail with Django's negative-indexing ValueError — two different behaviors for the same invalid input.
validated_findings.evidence: start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset
validated_findings.failure_mode: Inconsistent handling of invalid cursor input: silent wrong-page results in one path, unhandled exception in the other.
validated_findings.impact: Invalid cursors no longer surface as errors for forward paging (the first page is silently returned, and the derived next/prev cursors are computed from a different offset than requested), while prev cursors still fail with Django's negative-indexing ValueError — two different behaviors for the same invalid input.
validated_findings.root_cause: Partial offset normalization was added on one branch of a conditional expression while the prev-cursor path and the downstream `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check keep using the raw offset.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Handle negative offsets uniformly: validate once at the top of `get_result` and raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")` (as `OffsetPaginator` does) instead of clamping only the non-prev branch.
validated_findings.title: Silent clamping of negative offsets contradicts the added comment and is inconsistent for prev cursors
validated_findings.trigger: A client supplies a cursor with a negative offset to any `BasePaginator` subclass (e.g. `DateTimePaginator`). Forward cursors are now silently rewritten to offset 0, while prev cursors (`is_prev=True`) still pass the negative offset into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 182 shows `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` in BasePaginator. For is_prev=True with negative offset, the offset passes through unchanged. However, this is existing behavior in BasePaginator, not a new inconsistency introduced by this patch. The patch adds clamping for non-prev case which is an improvement.

validated_findings.trigger: Running `tests/sentry/api/test_paginator.py`, which contains no reference to `OptimizedCursorPaginator`; the class and its `enable_advanced_features` branch are exercised by no test.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Test gap for OptimizedCursorPaginator. While valid observation, test coverage gaps are process/style issues, not bugs with concrete runtime impact from the patch itself.

validated_findings.body: The ~60 copied lines will drift from the base implementation, so bug fixes and behavior changes silently apply to only one of the two paginators.
validated_findings.evidence: def get_result(self, limit=100, cursor=None, count_hits=False, known_hits=None, max_hits=None):
validated_findings.failure_mode: Divergent duplicated logic that defeats single-point maintenance.
validated_findings.impact: The ~60 copied lines will drift from the base implementation, so bug fixes and behavior changes silently apply to only one of the two paginators.
validated_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of the base class implementation instead of extending it via a narrow override.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Delete the copied body and instead override only the offset computation (e.g. extract a `_get_start_offset(cursor)` hook in `BasePaginator` and override it here), or drop the subclass entirely.
validated_findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates BasePaginator.get_result almost verbatim
validated_findings.trigger: Any future fix to `BasePaginator.get_result` (e.g. the offset handling changed earlier in this same patch at line 182, or the `post_query_filter` comment) must now be applied twice.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Code duplication between OptimizedCursorPaginator and BasePaginator is a style/maintainability concern, not a bug. No concrete runtime defect is identified.

validated_findings.body: Operators and developers debugging Redis will run SET commands (`SMEMBERS`, `SCARD`) against keys that are now sorted sets and get WRONGTYPE errors or wrong conclusions about the storage layout.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale documentation that misdescribes the on-disk/Redis data model.
validated_findings.impact: Operators and developers debugging Redis will run SET commands (`SMEMBERS`, `SCARD`) against keys that are now sorted sets and get WRONGTYPE errors or wrong conclusions about the storage layout.
validated_findings.root_cause: Data structure changed from set to sorted set without updating the accompanying storage-layout documentation.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Update the module docstring (and the add-buffer.lua header) to state that `span-buf:s:*` keys are sorted sets scored by `end_timestamp_precise`, with a 1000-member eviction cap.
validated_findings.title: Module docs still describe span buffer keys as Redis sets after switch to sorted sets
validated_findings.trigger: Reading the unchanged module documentation at src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:58 ("span-buf:s:* -- the actual set keys, containing span payloads") and :37 after this patch converts every `span-buf:s:*` key from a SET to a ZSET (`zadd`/`zscan`/`zunionstore`/`zcard`).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Documentation stating keys are 'sets' when they're now sorted sets is a doc defect. However, the claim about WRONGTYPE errors is speculative - operators would need to run wrong commands. The impact is low and the finding is about documentation staleness.

validated_findings.body: `KeyError: 'end_timestamp_precise'` is raised inside `process_batch`, crashing/stalling the span consumer for the whole batch rather than skipping the malformed span.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled KeyError halts span batch processing during producer/consumer version skew.
validated_findings.impact: `KeyError: 'end_timestamp_precise'` is raised inside `process_batch`, crashing/stalling the span consumer for the whole batch rather than skipping the malformed span.
validated_findings.root_cause: New required NamedTuple field is populated by direct dict indexing of an unvalidated JSON payload.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use a defensive read with a sensible default, e.g. `val.get("end_timestamp_precise") or timestamp`, or explicitly validate and route missing-field messages to the DLQ.
validated_findings.title: Required `end_timestamp_precise` read without fallback can crash the consumer on older payloads
validated_findings.trigger: Consuming an ingest-spans message that lacks `end_timestamp_precise` (e.g. messages already sitting in the topic from a producer version that omits it, or a relay rollout skew); `cast()` performs no runtime validation, unlike the sibling optional fields which use `val.get(...)`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 141 shows `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` using direct dict access. Unlike parent_span_id which uses val.get(), this will raise KeyError if the field is missing from older messages during version skew.
